Project Brief: Chrono-Bullet Hell

▼

Project Brief: Chrono-Bullet Hell

1.0 Project Overview

Project Name: Chrono-Bullet Hell
Genre: Time-Bending, Roguelike Bullet Hell
Elevator Pitch: Leap between timelines in a frantic roguelike shooter where every decision echoes. Dodge dense barrages of projectiles while manipulating time itself to outsmart foes and save a fractured future.
Target Audience: Fans of high-intensity, challenging, and replayable titles such as Enter the Gungeon, Hades, and Risk of Rain 2.

2.0 Core Gameplay Pillars

  • Bullet Hell Navigation: High-density projectile patterns requiring precise movement and offensive pressure.
  • Roguelike Loop: Procedurally generated room layouts, enemy encounters, and item drops. Permadeath is a core mechanic, with meta-progression tied to player stats and class unlocks.
  • Multi-Dimensional Time Manipulation:
    • Rewind: Reversal of player actions and state to correct tactical errors.
    • Slowdown: Reduction of velocity for all enemies and projectiles within the field.
    • Time Echoes: Creation of temporal clones that replay previous movement and attack inputs.
    • Timeline Leaping: Instant switching between two concurrent "World States" (Timeline A and B) to bypass hazards.
  • Class-Based Progression: Distinct starting weapons, health pools, and unique temporal abilities that define specific playstyles.

3.0 Technical Architecture & Systems

3.1 Temporal State Management

The game utilizes a Snapshot-based Circular Buffer to manage high-performance time manipulation:

  • Frequency: Snapshots recorded every 2–5 ticks (approx. every 60ms).
  • Window: A rolling 4–5 second history.
  • Data Captured: Player transforms, active projectile vectors, enemy health/positions, and current RNG seeds.
  • Deterministic Simulation: Projectile trajectories are calculated as a function of time (t). Rewinding rolls back the global "Chrono-Clock," resetting bullets based on the seed rather than tracking individual coordinate histories.

3.2 Time Echoes (Ghost Input System)

Echoes utilize a local input cache. Upon activation, an "Echo" entity reads movement and firing commands directly from the buffer. This allows the Echo to scale with the player's current weapon ID and active buffs without requiring AI pathfinding.

3.3 State Reconciliation & API Integration

  • Validation: The client performs local calculations and sends "Validated State" pulses to the API at the conclusion of a room or temporal effect.
  • Seed-Based Runs: Sessions are governed by a deterministic seed established in the initial_state to ensure server-side validation consistency.

4.0 Balancing & Difficulty (The "Temporal Friction" System)

  • Chrono-Meter: Energy source for Rewind and Echoes. This meter regenerates only when the player deals damage or "grazes" (narrowly dodges) enemy bullets.
  • Temporal Entropy (Debt): A penalty system where frequent time manipulation increases "Entropy." High Entropy triggers "Anomalous" enemy spawns, increased projectile speeds, and "Anomaly Orbs" that tether to the player.
  • Chronos-Locked Projectiles: Elite enemies fire purple-hued bullets immune to Rewind and Slowdown, requiring pure mechanical dodging.

5.0 Visual Style & Environments

Aesthetic: Stylized, high-tech aesthetic with vibrant, high-contrast color palettes for maximum readability.

  • Player Characters:
    • Chrono-Soldier: Lean, agile, futuristic suit with a visible temporal core.
    • Chrono-Gunner: Heavily armored, wielding massive multi-barreled weaponry.
  • Environments:
    • The Chrono-Nexus: A futuristic hub world.
    • Temporal Wastelands: Glitching, desolate battlegrounds.
    • The Clockwork Labyrinth: Surreal, gear-filled halls with non-Euclidean geometry.
  • VFX: Rewind creates visual "trails"; Slowdown triggers screen-wide desaturation; projectiles feature high-luminance dynamic trails.

6.0 Weapon Matrix

Weapon Name Class Damage Range Rate of Fire Ammo Notes
Chrono-Pistol All 10 Med 4/sec 50 Default, balanced.
Plasma Rifle Gunner 15 Long 6/sec 75 High damage, slow projectile.
Laser SMG Soldier 8 Short 10/sec 100 Rapid fire, close range.
Reality Ripper All 30 Long Cont. 200 Hits both timelines.
Chrono-Blade Soldier 50 Melee 2/sec N/A High risk, high damage.
Time Grenade All 25 Area 1/sec 5 Slows enemies in radius.
Singularity Cannon All 60 V. Long 1 (chg) 1 Massive damage, slow charge.

7.0 Data Structures

7.1 Database Schema

  1. Players: player_id, player_name, total_runs, runs_won, unlocked_classes (JSON).
  2. Classes: class_id, class_name, starting_weapon_id, special_ability, entropy_resistance.
  3. Weapons: weapon_id, weapon_name, damage_per_hit, rate_of_fire, effect_description.
  4. Runs: run_id, player_id, start_timestamp, run_duration, run_successful, seed.

7.2 API Endpoints

  • GET /api/player/{id}: Fetch profile and meta-progression.
  • POST /api/runs/new: Initialize a run with a specific class and seed.
  • PUT /api/runs/{id}: Update "Validated State" (health, position, room clears).
  • DELETE /api/runs/{id}: Finalize run and log duration.

8.0 MVP Feature Specifications

US-001: Rewind Mechanic

  • Given: The player has at least 25% Chrono-Meter and the snapshot buffer contains 4 seconds of history.
  • When: The player presses the 'Rewind' input.
  • Then: The player's position, health, and ammo count revert to the state recorded 3 seconds prior, and the Chrono-Meter is depleted by 25%.

US-002: Timeline Leaping

  • Given: The player is currently in 'Timeline A' and the 'Timeline Leap' ability is off cooldown.
  • When: The player triggers the 'Timeline Leap' command.
  • Then: The environment assets and enemy spawns swap to the 'Timeline B' state while maintaining the player's relative screen coordinates.

US-003: Temporal Entropy Scaling

  • Given: The player's current 'Entropy' level is 80 or higher.
  • When: A new room encounter is generated.
  • Then: The system spawns at least one 'Anomalous' enemy variant with 1.5x health and increased projectile speed.

US-004: Seed-Based Generation

  • Given: A new run is initialized via the POST /api/runs/new endpoint.
  • When: The client receives the initial_state containing a specific integer seed.
  • Then: All procedural room layouts and item drops must be generated deterministically based on that seed.

US-005: Chrono-Meter Regeneration

  • Given: The player's Chrono-Meter is below 100%.
  • When: The player's hitbox enters the "Graze" radius of an enemy projectile without taking damage.
  • Then: The Chrono-Meter increases by 2%.

Pitch Deck

▼

SLIDE 1: Title Slide

Chrono-Bullet Hell

A Time-Bending, Roguelike Shooter

Where every decision echoes through time.

SLIDE 2: The Problem

The roguelike and bullet hell genres thrive on high-intensity, replayable challenges. However, many titles lack innovative mechanics that truly break the mold. Players seek fresh strategic layers that go beyond simple pattern recognition and resource management, offering deeper tactical choices and a more dynamic combat experience.

SLIDE 3: The Solution: Your Project

Chrono-Bullet Hell is a fast-paced, roguelike shooter that introduces a unique multi-dimensional time manipulation system. Players will leap between timelines, rewind their mistakes, and create temporal echoes to outsmart dense barrages of projectiles. It offers a highly replayable, challenging, and strategically deep experience for fans of the genre.

SLIDE 4: Core Features & Loop

The core loop revolves around intense, procedurally generated bullet hell encounters where the player's primary tool is time itself.

  • Bullet Hell Navigation: Precise movement against dense, challenging projectile patterns.
  • Roguelike Loop: Permadeath, procedural generation, and meta-progression for infinite replayability.
  • Time Manipulation: Rewind mistakes, slow down time, create temporal clones (Echoes), and leap between two distinct timelines to bypass hazards and gain tactical advantages.
  • Class-Based Progression: Four unique classes with distinct playstyles and special abilities.

SLIDE 5: Unique Selling Proposition

Our game distinguishes itself through its innovative and deeply integrated time manipulation mechanics, particularly the 'Timeline Leaping' and 'Time Echoes' features. This provides a strategic depth and dynamic combat feel unmatched in the genre, offering a fresh take on the high-intensity, replayable roguelike formula.

SLIDE 6: Target Audience

Our target audience is core gamers aged 18-35 who enjoy challenging, skill-based, and replayable titles. This includes fans of existing roguelikes and bullet hell shooters such as Enter the Gungeon, Hades, and Risk of Rain 2. The market for high-quality, innovative indie titles in these genres remains strong and engaged.

SLIDE 7: Art & Style

The game will feature a stylized, high-tech aesthetic with a focus on high-contrast color palettes for maximum readability during intense combat. Player characters will be distinct and easily identifiable, while environments will be surreal and dynamic, reflecting the temporal distortions of the game world.

MVP Definition

▼

Summary

This document outlines the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) for 'Chrono-Bullet Hell', a time-bending, roguelike shooter. The MVP focuses on establishing the core gameplay loop and unique temporal mechanics, including Rewind, Timeline Leaping, and the Chrono-Meter system. It also defines the initial player classes, weapon set, and the data structures required for progression and state management. The goal is to deliver a challenging, replayable, and mechanically deep experience that sets the foundation for future development.

In Scope

  • ✓ Core Gameplay Loop (Roguelike, Bullet Hell)
  • ✓ Player Movement & Combat
  • ✓ Rewind Mechanic (US-001)
  • ✓ Timeline Leaping Mechanic (US-002)
  • ✓ Chrono-Meter System (Regeneration, Cost)
  • ✓ Temporal Entropy System (Basic Scaling, US-003)
  • ✓ Initial 2 Player Classes (Chrono-Soldier, Chrono-Gunner)
  • ✓ Initial Weapon Set (Chrono-Pistol, Plasma Rifle, Laser SMG, Time Grenade)
  • ✓ Seed-Based Procedural Generation (US-004)
  • ✓ Basic Meta-Progression (Class Unlocks)
  • ✓ Core Data Structures (Players, Classes, Weapons)
  • ✓ Essential API Endpoints (New Run, Update State, Finalize Run)
  • ✓ Visual Style & VFX (Core effects for time manipulation)
  • ✓ Chrono-Meter Regeneration (US-005)

Out of Scope

  • ✕ All other temporal mechanics (Time Echoes, Slowdown)
  • ✕ All other player classes and weapons
  • ✕ Advanced Temporal Entropy effects (Anomalous Orbs, Chronos-Locked Projectiles)
  • ✕ Full narrative content and lore
  • ✕ Complex environment design and non-Euclidean geometry
  • ✕ Detailed player progression systems (e.g., stat upgrades)
  • ✕ Multiplayer functionality
  • ✕ Full weapon matrix and item pool
  • ✕ Comprehensive API for all game systems
  • ✕ Advanced UI/UX for time manipulation
  • ✕ Full database schema implementation and server infrastructure

MVP Feature Specifications

▼

Core Gameplay Loop (Roguelike, Bullet Hell)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player successfully rewinds time Given the player has at least 1 'Rewind' charge available When the player activates the 'Rewind' ability Then the player's position and state are reset to what they were 5 seconds prior, and 1 'Rewind' charge is consumed.

US-002: Player fails to rewind time due to insufficient charge Given the player has 0 'Rewind' charges available When the player attempts to activate the 'Rewind' ability Then the ability fails to activate, and no charge is consumed.

US-003: Player successfully dodges a single bullet Given a single enemy bullet is traveling directly towards the player When the player performs a successful dodge maneuver just before impact Then the player's character is briefly invulnerable and moves out of the bullet's path.

US-004: Player is hit by a single bullet Given the player is not currently invulnerable When a single enemy bullet successfully hits the player's character model Then the player's health is reduced by the bullet's damage value.

US-005: Player collects a health pickup Given the player's current health is less than their maximum health When the player walks over a health pickup item on the ground Then the player's health is increased by a fixed amount, and the pickup item is removed from the map.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Core Gameplay Loop & State Management

1. Overview

This specification defines the fundamental data structures and state management required for the core roguelike and time-bending gameplay loop.

2. Data Structures

2.1. Player State (playerState)

This object holds all dynamic information about the player's current run.

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
runId String A unique identifier for the current game run. Used for saving and loading. Yes UUID format.
playerClass String The ID of the player's chosen class. Yes References the playerClasses table.
health Float The player's current health. Cannot exceed maxHealth. Yes Must be clamped between 0 and maxHealth.
maxHealth Float The player's maximum health value, determined by their class. Yes Defined in playerClasses.
rewindCharges Integer The number of times the player can use the Rewind ability. Yes Resets to maxRewindCharges on death.
maxRewindCharges Integer The maximum number of Rewind charges the player can hold. Yes Defined by the player's class.
chronoMeter Float The player's resource for time abilities. Yes Must be clamped between 0 and 100.
maxChronoMeter Float The maximum value of the Chrono-Meter. Yes Defined by the player's class.
currentWeapon String The ID of the weapon the player is currently wielding. Yes References the weapons table.
inventory Array of Strings A list of weapon IDs the player is carrying. Yes Includes the currentWeapon.
position Vector2 The player's current X, Y coordinates in the level. Yes Updated every frame.
levelSeed String The seed used to procedurally generate the current level. Yes Used for saving/loading and replay.
isInvulnerable Boolean Flag indicating if the player is currently immune to damage. Yes Set to true for a short duration after taking damage or dodging.
invulnerabilityTimer Float The remaining duration of the invulnerability state. Yes Ticks down when isInvulnerable is true.

2.2. Player Class Definition (playerClasses)

This table defines the base stats and abilities for each player class.

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
classId String A unique identifier for the class (e.g., "chronoSoldier"). Yes Primary key.
className String The display name of the class. Yes
baseHealth Float The starting and maximum health for this class. Yes
baseMaxRewindCharges Integer The maximum number of Rewind charges for this class. Yes
baseMaxChronoMeter Float The maximum value of the Chrono-Meter for this class. Yes
chronoMeterRegenRate Float The rate at which the Chrono-Meter regenerates per second. Yes
dodgeInvulnerabilityDuration Float The duration of invulnerability granted by a successful dodge. Yes
startingWeapon String The ID of the weapon the player begins with. Yes

2.3. Weapon Definition (weapons)

This table defines the properties of each weapon. Note that this is a simplified list for the MVP. A full game would have many more weapons.

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
weaponId String A unique identifier for the weapon (e.g., "plasmaRifle"). Yes Primary key.
weaponName String The display name of the weapon. Yes
damage Float The amount of damage the weapon deals per shot. Yes
fireRate Float The time in seconds between shots. Yes
bulletSpeed Float The speed at which the projectile travels. Yes
ammoType String The type of ammo required (e.g., "energy", "bullet"). Yes
maxAmmo Integer The maximum number of shots the player can carry for this weapon. Yes
isTimeBased Boolean True if the weapon has special time-based properties. Yes
timeCostPerShot Float The amount of Chrono-Meter consumed per shot if isTimeBased is true. Yes

2.4. Level Configuration (levelConfig)

Configuration data for level generation.

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
roomCount Integer The total number of rooms in the level. Yes
minEnemiesPerRoom Integer The minimum number of enemies to spawn in a room. Yes
maxEnemiesPerRoom Integer The maximum number of enemies to spawn in a room. Yes
pickupSpawnRate Float The probability of a health pickup spawning in a room. Yes

3. Core System Logic

3.1. Player Movement

Standard WASD or controller input. The player can perform a quick dodge (e.g., Spacebar/Button) that grants brief invulnerability. The dodge consumes a Rewind charge if available, otherwise it is free but has a cooldown.

3.2. Combat

Player aims with the mouse/right stick and fires with the left click/trigger. Firing a time-based weapon consumes Chrono-Meter.

3.3. Rewind (US-001)

When activated, the game saves the last 5 seconds of player state (position, health, ammo, etc.). Upon use, the game reverts to that saved state. Consumes 1 Rewind charge. If no charges are available, the ability fails (US-002).

3.4. Chrono-Meter Management (US-005)

The Chrono-Meter regenerates slowly over time, with the rate determined by the player's class. Firing time-based weapons consumes the meter. Collecting health pickups also restores a portion of the meter.

3.5. Temporal Entropy (US-003)

This is a high-level concept for scaling difficulty. The levelConfig will be dynamically adjusted based on the player's progress (e.g., number of rooms completed). This will affect enemy spawn rates, enemy types, and potentially the availability of pickups. The playerState.isInvulnerable flag is the most basic form of temporal manipulation for the player.

4. API Endpoints (Conceptual)

4.1. POST /new_run

Starts a new game. Takes the playerClass and levelSeed as input. Returns the initial playerState.

4.2. POST /update_state

Called frequently to save the player's current state (position, health, etc.) during a run.

4.3. POST /use_rewind

Activates the Rewind ability. Checks for charge availability and performs the state rollback. Returns the new playerState.

4.4. POST /finalize_run

Called when the player dies or completes the game. Saves the final playerState for meta-progression tracking.

5. Visual Style & VFX

  • Rewind: A screen-space effect that briefly shows a ghost of the player's past position before snapping back.
  • Dodge: A quick, invulnerability-granting dash with a short trail effect.
  • Time-Based Weapons: Unique visual effects that clearly communicate their Chrono-Meter cost.
  • Chrono-Meter UI: A prominent UI element that clearly displays the player's current Chrono-Meter level and maximum capacity.

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player Successfully Rewinds Time

Scenario 1: Player successfully rewinds time Given the player has 3 'Rewind' charges available When the player activates the 'Rewind' ability Then the player's position and state are reset to what they were 5 seconds ago, and their charge count decreases to 2.

Scenario 2: Player attempts to rewind with no charges Given the player has 0 'Rewind' charges available When the player attempts to activate the 'Rewind' ability Then the ability fails to activate, and no charge is consumed.

US-002: Player Successfully Uses Time Stop

Scenario 1: Player successfully stops time Given the player has 1 'Time Stop' charge available When the player activates the 'Time Stop' ability Then all enemies and projectiles in the level are frozen for 3 seconds, and their charge count decreases to 0.

Scenario 2: Player attempts to stop time with no charges Given the player has 0 'Time Stop' charges available When the player attempts to activate the 'Time Stop' ability Then the ability fails to activate, and no charge is consumed.

US-003: Player Successfully Dodges an Attack

Scenario 1: Player successfully dodges an attack Given an enemy projectile is traveling towards the player When the player performs a successful dodge maneuver Then the player is moved 3 meters to the side, and the projectile misses them.

Rewind Mechanic (US-001)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001

Scenario 1: Player successfully rewinds time Given the player has at least 1 charge of the Rewind ability. When the player activates the Rewind ability. Then the player's position and state are reset to what they were 3 seconds prior, and their Rewind charge is reduced by 1.

Scenario 2: Player cannot rewind with insufficient charges Given the player has 0 charges of the Rewind ability. When the player attempts to activate the Rewind ability. Then the ability should not trigger, and a 'not enough charges' feedback message should be displayed.

Scenario 3: Rewind charge is replenished over time Given the player has 0 charges of the Rewind ability. When 60 seconds pass in the game. Then the player's Rewind charge should be fully restored to 3.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Rewind Mechanic Technical Specification

1. Overview

This document details the technical implementation of the Rewind mechanic, a core feature of Chrono-Bullet Hell. The system allows the player to reverse their own state and the immediate environment for a short duration.

2. System Architecture

The Rewind mechanic will be managed by a dedicated RewindManager component. This manager will be responsible for recording the player's state over time and executing the rewind sequence.

3. Data Structures

3.1. Rewind State Frame

This structure defines a single point in the player's history that can be rewound to.

Field Name Type Description
timestamp Float The game time at which this state frame was recorded.
position Vector3 The player's world position at the time of recording.
rotation Quaternion The player's world rotation at the time of recording.
health Float The player's health at the time of recording.
rewindCharges Int The number of Rewind charges the player had at the time of recording.
isGrounded Boolean The player's grounded state at the time of recording.
currentWeapon String The name of the currently equipped weapon at the time of recording.
ammo Object A key-value map of weapon names to their ammo counts at the time of recording.

3.2. Rewind Manager State

This data structure holds the current state of the Rewind system.

Field Name Type Description
maxCharges Int The maximum number of Rewind charges the player can hold (e.g., 3).
currentCharges Int The player's current number of Rewind charges.
chargeRechargeTime Float The time in seconds required to restore one charge (e.g., 60.0).
rewindDuration Float The duration of the rewind in seconds (e.g., 3.0).
stateFrames Array of Rewind State Frame A list or queue containing the last rewindDuration seconds of player state.
isRewinding Boolean A flag indicating if the rewind sequence is currently active.
rewindStartTime Float The game time at which the current rewind sequence began.

4. Core Logic

4.1. State Recording

At a fixed interval (e.g., every 0.1 seconds), the RewindManager will record the current player state (position, rotation, health, etc.) into a new Rewind State Frame and add it to the stateFrames list. If the list exceeds the capacity for the rewindDuration, the oldest frame is removed.

4.2. Rewind Activation

When the player presses the Rewind button:

  1. The system checks if currentCharges > 0 and isRewinding is false.
  2. If checks pass, currentCharges is decremented.
  3. The isRewinding flag is set to true.
  4. The rewindStartTime is set to the current game time.
  5. The RewindManager searches the stateFrames list for the frame that occurred exactly rewindDuration seconds ago. If no frame exists (e.g., the player hasn't been alive long enough), it uses the oldest available frame.
  6. The player's state (position, rotation, health, etc.) is immediately set to match the found Rewind State Frame.
  7. The RewindManager begins a countdown for the rewindDuration. During this time, it will not record new state frames.
  8. Once the rewindDuration countdown is complete, isRewinding is set to false, and the normal state recording process resumes.

4.3. Charge Recharging

The RewindManager will have a separate timer for each charge. When a charge is used, its recharge timer starts. When a timer reaches zero, the charge is restored to currentCharges, up to maxCharges. This timer should be independent of the isRewinding state.

Timeline Leaping Mechanic (US-002)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player successfully rewinds time Given the player has at least 1 'Rewind Charge' available When the player activates the 'Rewind' ability Then the player's position and state are reset to what they were 3 seconds prior.

US-002: Player attempts to rewind with no charges Given the player has 0 'Rewind Charges' available When the player attempts to activate the 'Rewind' ability Then the ability fails to activate and a visual/audio cue indicates it is unavailable.

US-003: Player rewinds into a hazard Given the player is standing on a floor tile that will become a lava pit in 2 seconds When the player activates the 'Rewind' ability (which rewinds 3 seconds) Then the player is placed back on the floor tile, but the lava pit does not yet exist.

Player Data\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| playerID | String | Unique identifier for the player. |\n| currentClass | String | The ID of the currently equipped player class. |\n| rewindCharges | Integer | The number of available Rewind uses. Must be >= 0. |\n| maxRewindCharges | Integer | The maximum number of Rewind charges the player can hold. |\n| chronoMeter | Float | The current charge level of the Chrono-Meter (0.0 to 1.0). |\n| maxChronoMeter | Float | The maximum charge level of the Chrono-Meter. |\n| currentWeaponID | String | The ID of the currently equipped weapon. |\n| inventory | Array | A list of IDs for all weapons the player is carrying. |\n| metaProgression | Object | A data structure to store all unlocked content. |\n| metaProgression.classes | Array | A list of all player class IDs that the player has unlocked. |\n| metaProgression.weapons | Array | A list of all weapon IDs that the player has unlocked. |\n\n### 2. Player Class Data\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| classID | String | Unique identifier for the class (e.g., 'Chrono-Soldier'). |\n| name | String | The display name of the class. |\n| description | String | A short description of the class's playstyle. |\n| startingWeaponID | String | The ID of the weapon the player starts with. |\n| startingInventory | Array | A list of all weapon IDs the player starts with. |\n| baseMaxRewindCharges | Integer | The base number of Rewind charges for this class. |\n| baseMaxChronoMeter | Float | The base maximum charge for the Chrono-Meter for this class. |\n| baseChronoMeterRegenRate | Float | The base rate at which the Chrono-Meter regenerates per second. |\n\n### 3. Weapon Data\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| weaponID | String | Unique identifier for the weapon (e.g., 'Laser_SMG'). |\n| name | String | The display name of the weapon. |\n| description | String | A short description of the weapon's function. |\n| type | String | The type of weapon (e.g., 'SMG', 'Grenade'). |\n| damage | Float | The base damage dealt per hit/explosion. |\n| fireRate | Float | The time in seconds between shots. |\n| ammoCapacity | Integer | The maximum number of shots the weapon can hold. |\n| rewindCost | Integer | The number of Rewind charges consumed to fire this weapon. |\n| isTimeWeapon | Boolean | True if the weapon has special time-manipulating properties. |\n\n### 4. Game State Data\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| gameSeed | String | The seed used to generate the current run's procedural content. |\n| currentLevelID | String | The ID of the current level. |\n| playerState | Object | A snapshot of the player's state at a specific point in time for Rewind. |\n| playerState.position | Vector3 | The player's world position. |\n| playerState.rotation | Quaternion | The player's world rotation. |\n| playerState.health | Integer | The player's current health. |\n| playerState.rewindCharges | Integer | The player's current Rewind charges. |\n| playerState.chronoMeter | Float | The player's current Chrono-Meter charge. |\n| playerState.inventory | Array | The player's current weapon inventory. |\n| playerState.currentWeaponID | String | The player's currently equipped weapon. |\n| temporalEntropyLevel | Integer | The current scaling level of the Temporal Entropy system. |\n\n## TS-002: Core Gameplay Systems\n\n### 1. Rewind Mechanic\n\n* Functionality: Upon activation, the game rewinds the player's state (position, rotation, health, charges, meter, inventory) to a specific point in the past (e.g., 3 seconds). The player is placed at that past position.

  • Constraints: Can only be used if rewindCharges > 0. Consumes one charge.
  • State Preservation: The player's current weapon and ammo are preserved.
  • Temporal Entropy Interaction: The player is placed back on the floor tile as it was at that past moment. If the floor tile was a hazard in the present but not in the past, the player will not be standing on the hazard.
  • Data Structure: Requires a history stack of PlayerState objects.

2. Timeline Leaping Mechanic\n\n* Functionality: Upon activation, the player instantly teleports to a new, randomly selected location on the current level.

  • Constraints: Consumes a significant portion of the Chrono-Meter (e.g., 50%). Cannot be used if the Chrono-Meter is below the cost.
  • State Preservation: Player's current weapon, ammo, health, charges, and meter are preserved.
  • Data Structure: Requires a function to select a valid, non-obstructed destination point on the current level's navmesh.

3. Chrono-Meter System\n\n* Functionality: A resource used to fuel powerful temporal abilities.

  • Generation:
    • Passive Regeneration: The meter regenerates at a base rate defined by the player's class, modified by Temporal Entropy.
    • Damage Bonus: A small amount of meter is granted for every point of damage the player takes.
  • Cost: Used by the Timeline Leaping mechanic.
  • Data Structure: A single float variable chronoMeter and associated constants for base regeneration rate and damage bonus.

4. Temporal Entropy System\n\n* Functionality: A scaling difficulty system that increases the challenge as the player progresses through the run.

  • Progression: The temporalEntropyLevel increases after completing each level.
  • Effects (MVP):
    • Increases the cost of the Timeline Leaping mechanic.
    • Increases the base Chrono-Meter regeneration rate (to compensate for increased cost).
    • Increases the number of enemies spawned in subsequent levels.
  • Data Structure: An integer temporalEntropyLevel and a lookup table to map the level to specific gameplay modifiers.

TS-003: API Endpoints (Server-Side / State Management)\n\n* /newRun

*   **Method:** POST
*   **Description:** Starts a new game run.
*   **Request Body:** `{ "playerClassID": "...", "gameSeed": "..." }`
*   **Response Body:** `{ "runID": "...", "initialPlayerState": { ... } }`
  • /updateState
    • Method: POST
    • Description: Called periodically or after significant events to save the player's current state for the current run.
    • Request Body: { "runID": "...", "playerState": { ... } }
    • Response Body: { "success": true }
  • /finalizeRun
    • Method: POST
    • Description: Called when the player dies or completes the final level. Records the run's outcome and updates meta-progression.
    • Request Body: { "runID": "...", "outcome": "death/completion", "score": 12345 }
    • Response Body: { "metaProgressionUpdate": { "unlockedClasses": ["..."], "unlockedWeapons": ["..."] } }
  • /getMetaProgression
    • Method: GET
    • Description: Retrieves the player's current meta-progression data.
    • Response Body: `{ "unlockedClasses": ["..."], "unlockedWeapons": ["..."] }

Chrono-Meter System (Regeneration, Cost)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player successfully rewinds time Given the player has 100 Chrono-Meter units and the rewind ability is ready When the player activates the rewind ability Then the player's position and state are reverted to 5 seconds prior, and 20 Chrono-Meter units are consumed.

US-002: Player attempts to rewind with insufficient meter Given the player has only 15 Chrono-Meter units When the player attempts to activate the rewind ability (which costs 20 units) Then the rewind ability does not activate, and a visual/audio cue indicates it is not ready.

US-003: Chrono-Meter regeneration over time Given the player has 50 Chrono-Meter units When 10 seconds pass without the player using any Chrono-Meter abilities Then the player's Chrono-Meter should have increased to a value greater than 50 (e.g., 70).

US-004: Chrono-Meter cost for a special attack Given the player has 80 Chrono-Meter units and the 'Bullet Time' ability is ready When the player activates the 'Bullet Time' ability (which costs 60 units) Then the player's Chrono-Meter should be reduced to 20 units, and the 'Bullet Time' effect should begin.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Chrono-Meter System - Data Structure

1. Overview

This specification defines the data structure for the Chrono-Meter, the primary resource for all time-manipulation abilities.

2. Data Table

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
currentValue float The current amount of Chrono-Meter units the player possesses. Yes Must be between 0 and maxValue.
maxValue float The maximum number of Chrono-Meter units the player can hold. Yes This value can be increased through meta-progression.
regenerationRate float The amount of Chrono-Meter units gained per second when not using abilities. Yes Measured in units/second.
lastAbilityUseTime float A timestamp of the last time any Chrono-Meter ability was used. Yes Used to determine when to start regeneration.
rewindCost float The specific number of units required to activate the Rewind ability. Yes As per US-001, this is 20.
bulletTimeCost float The specific number of units required to activate the Bullet Time ability. Yes As per US-004, this is 60.
rewindDuration float The duration of the Rewind effect in seconds. Yes As per US-001, this is 5.
bulletTimeDuration float The duration of the Bullet Time effect in seconds. Yes As per US-004, this is 60.

TS-002: Player State - Core Data Structure

1. Overview

This specification defines the core data structure that holds all persistent and temporary state information for a single player character.

2. Data Table

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
playerID string A unique identifier for the player. Yes UUID format.
currentClass string The name of the player's currently selected class. Yes References a class defined in PlayerClassData.
chronoMeter object A nested object containing all Chrono-Meter data. Yes See TS-001 for the schema of this object.
health float The player's current health points. Yes Must be between 0 and maxHealth.
maxHealth float The maximum health points the player can have. Yes Can be increased through meta-progression.
position object The player's current position in 3D space. Yes Contains x, y, z float values.
rotation object The player's current rotation in 3D space. Yes Contains yaw, pitch, roll float values.
inventory array A list of the player's currently held items. Yes Contains item IDs or data.
unlockedClasses array A list of the names of all player classes that have been unlocked. Yes Used for meta-progression.

TS-003: Player Class Data - Configuration

1. Overview

This specification defines the data structure for player class configurations, which dictate their unique stats and abilities.

2. Data Table

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
className string The unique name of the player class. Yes e.g., "Chrono-Soldier".
description string A short description of the class's lore and playstyle. Yes
baseHealth float The starting health for this class. Yes
baseMaxHealth float The maximum health for this class. Yes
baseChronoMeterMax float The maximum Chrono-Meter capacity for this class. Yes
baseChronoMeterRegen float The base regeneration rate for this class. Yes
startingWeapon string The ID of the weapon the player starts with. Yes References a weapon in WeaponData.
abilities array A list of the abilities available to this class. Yes Contains ability IDs and their specific costs/durations.

TS-004: Weapon Data - Configuration

1. Overview

This specification defines the data structure for all weapons in the game.

2. Data Table

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
weaponID string A unique identifier for the weapon. Yes e.g., "PlasmaRifle".
weaponName string The display name of the weapon. Yes
description string A short description of the weapon. Yes
weaponType string The type of weapon (e.g., "Rifle", "SMG", "Grenade"). Yes Used for damage calculations and ammo types.
damage float The base damage dealt by a single hit or explosion. Yes
fireRate float The time in seconds between shots. Yes 0 for instant-hit or explosive weapons.
ammoType string The type of ammo the weapon uses. Yes e.g., "Plasma", "Laser".
maxAmmo int The maximum number of shots the player can carry for this ammo type. Yes
baseMaxReserveAmmo int The maximum number of shots the player can carry for this ammo type. Yes This value can be increased through meta-progression.
projectileSpeed float The speed at which the weapon's projectile travels. Yes 0 for hitscan weapons.
range float The maximum effective range of the weapon. Yes 0 for melee or explosive weapons.
isTimeAbilityWeapon boolean Flag indicating if this weapon consumes Chrono-Meter. Yes Set to true for the Time Grenade.
chronoMeterCost float The amount of Chrono-Meter consumed when firing this weapon. Yes 0 if isTimeAbilityWeapon is false.

TS-005: Temporal Entropy System - Configuration

1. Overview

This specification defines the data for the Temporal Entropy system, which scales the game's difficulty over time.

2. Data Table

Field Name Data Type Description Required Notes
entropyLevel int The current level of temporal entropy. Yes Starts at 1.
maxEntropyLevel int The maximum possible entropy level. Yes
timeToNextLevel float The amount of time in seconds required to advance to the next entropy level. Yes This value increases at higher entropy levels.
healthRegenMultiplier float A multiplier applied to the player's base health regeneration rate at this entropy level. Yes As per US-003, this should be less than 1.0.
enemySpawnRateMultiplier float A multiplier applied to the base enemy spawn rate. Yes Should increase with entropy.
chronoMeterRegenMultiplier float A multiplier applied to the player's base Chrono-Meter regeneration rate. Yes Should decrease with entropy.

Temporal Entropy System (Basic Scaling, US-003)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-003: Temporal Entropy System (Basic Scaling)

Scenario 1: Entropy increases after a player death

Given the player is in a match with a current Entropy level of 5% When the player is killed by an enemy Then the match's Entropy level should increase to 10%

Scenario 2: Entropy increases after a long time without player death

Given the player has survived for 2 minutes without dying When the 2-minute survival timer expires Then the match's Entropy level should increase to 15%

Scenario 3: Entropy increases after a player kill

Given the player has just killed an enemy When the kill event is processed Then the match's Entropy level should increase by 2%

Player Class Data\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| classId | String | Unique identifier for the class (e.g., "Chrono-Soldier"). |\n| name | String | The display name of the class. |\n| description | String | A short description of the class's lore and playstyle. |\n| baseHealth | Float | The player's base health value. |\n| baseChronoMeterCapacity | Float | The player's base Chrono-Meter capacity. |\n| baseChronoMeterRegenRate | Float | The player's base Chrono-Meter regeneration rate per second. |\n| startingWeaponId | String | The ID of the weapon the player begins with. |\n\n### 3. Weapon Data\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| weaponId | String | Unique identifier for the weapon (e.g., "Laser_SMG"). |\n| name | String | The display name of the weapon. |\n| description | String | A short description of the weapon. |\n| type | String | The type of weapon (e.g., "SMG", "Grenade"). |\n| damage | Float | The base damage dealt by a single hit or explosion. |\n| fireRate | Float | The time in seconds between shots. |\n| ammoCapacity | Integer | The maximum number of shots the weapon can hold. |\n| isTimeWeapon | Boolean | True if the weapon has a special time-related effect. |\n| timeCost | Float | The Chrono-Meter cost to use the weapon (if isTimeWeapon is true). |\n\n### 4. Match State Data\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| matchId | String | Unique identifier for the current match. |\n| playerId | String | The ID of the player in the match. |\n| currentEntropy | Float | The current percentage of Temporal Entropy (0.0 to 1.0). |\n| survivalTimer | Float | The time in seconds remaining on the current survival timer. |\n| playerState | String | The current state of the player (e.g., "Alive", "Dead"). |\n| currentWeaponId | String | The ID of the weapon the player is currently holding. |\n| playerHealth | Float | The player's current health. |\n| playerChronoMeter | Float | The player's current Chrono-Meter charge. |\n\n## TS-002: Core API Endpoints\n\n### 1. POST /match/start\n\nDescription: Initiates a new match for the player.\n\nRequest Body:\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| playerId | String | The ID of the player starting the match. |\n| classId | String | The ID of the player's chosen class. |\n\nResponse Body:\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| matchId | String | The unique ID for the new match. |\n| initialMatchState | Object | The complete starting state of the match (see Match State Data). |\n\n### 2. POST /match/update\n\nDescription: Called periodically to update the game state for a match.\n\nRequest Body:\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| matchId | String | The ID of the current match. |\n| playerInput | Object | A snapshot of the player's inputs (e.g., movement vectors, button presses). |\n| deltaSeconds | Float | The time elapsed since the last update. |\n\nResponse Body:\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| newMatchState | Object | The updated state of the match. |\n\n### 3. POST /match/end\n\nDescription: Finalizes a match and processes the results.\n\nRequest Body:\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| matchId | String | The ID of the completed match. |\n| playerId | String | The ID of the player whose match ended. |\n| win | Boolean | True if the player won the match, false otherwise. |\n| score | Integer | The player's final score. |\n\nResponse Body:\n\n| Field Name | Data Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| unlockedItems | Array of Strings | A list of any new items or classes unlocked as a result of the match. |\n\n## TS-003: Temporal Entropy System (Core Logic)\n\n### 1. Entropy Increase Events\n\n* Player Death: When a player's health reaches zero, the currentEntropy for that match is increased by a fixed amount (e.g., 0.05 or 5%).

  • Time Without Death: A continuous timer is active. If a player survives for a set duration without dying (e.g., 120 seconds), the currentEntropy is increased by a fixed amount (e.g., 0.10 or 10%). This timer resets upon player death.
  • Player Kill: When a player successfully kills an enemy, the currentEntropy for that match is increased by a small, fixed amount (e.g., 0.02 or 2%).
  • Entropy Cap: The currentEntropy value will not exceed a maximum threshold (e.g., 1.0 or 100%).

2. Entropy State Management

  • The currentEntropy value is a global state for the match.
  • It is a float value between 0.0 and 1.0.
  • It is included in every POST /match/update response to the client.
  • The value is used to trigger the Temporal Entropy effects defined in other technical specifications.

3. Reset Condition

  • The currentEntropy value is reset to 0.0 at the start of every new match.
  • The survival timer is reset to its initial value upon player death.

TS-004: Chrono-Meter System (Core Logic)\n\n### 1. Chrono-Meter States

  • The Chrono-Meter is a resource that players use to activate special abilities.
  • It is a float value between 0.0 and baseChronoMeterCapacity.

2. Regeneration

  • The Chrono-Meter regenerates over time at a rate defined by baseChronoMeterRegenRate.
  • The regeneration rate is a constant value and is not affected by the Temporal Entropy level in this MVP.

3. Consumption

  • Using a special ability (e.g., Rewind, Timeline Leaping) consumes a specific amount of Chrono-Meter charge.
  • The cost is defined by the ability's data (e.g., rewindCost).
  • A player cannot use an ability if they do not have enough Chrono-Meter charge.

4. Reset Condition

  • The Chrono-Meter is fully refilled to baseChronoMeterCapacity at the start of every new match.
  • The Chrono-Meter is also fully refilled upon the player's death.

Initial 2 Player Classes (Chrono-Soldier, Chrono-Gunner)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Chrono-Soldier - Basic Rewind

Scenario 1: Player successfully rewinds time Given the Chrono-Soldier has 3 'Rewind' charges available When the player activates the 'Rewind' ability Then the player's position and health are restored to their state 5 seconds prior.

Scenario 2: Player cannot rewind with no charges Given the Chrono-Soldier has 0 'Rewind' charges available When the player attempts to activate the 'Rewind' ability Then the ability fails to activate and a 'charge unavailable' message is displayed.

Scenario 3: Rewind charge is on cooldown Given the Chrono-Soldier has just used their 'Rewind' ability When the player attempts to activate 'Rewind' again immediately Then the ability fails to activate and a 'cooldown active' message is displayed.

US-002: Chrono-Soldier - Rewind with Damage

Scenario 1: Player rewinds after taking damage Given the Chrono-Soldier has 3 'Rewind' charges available and is at 50/100 health When the player takes 20 damage (health is now 30/100) and then immediately activates 'Rewind' Then the player's health is restored to 50/100 and their position is rewound by 5 seconds.

US-003: Chrono-Gunner - Basic Time Stop

Scenario 1: Player successfully stops time Given the Chrono-Gunner has 3 'Time Stop' charges available When the player activates the 'Time Stop' ability Then time for all enemies and projectiles freezes for 4 seconds.

Scenario 2: Player cannot stop time with no charges Given the Chrono-Gunner has 0 'Time Stop' charges available When the player attempts to activate the 'Time Stop' ability Then the ability fails to activate and a 'charge unavailable' message is displayed.

Scenario 3: Time Stop charge is on cooldown Given the Chrono-Gunner has just used their 'Time Stop' ability When the player attempts to activate 'Time Stop' again immediately Then the ability fails to activate and a 'cooldown active' message is displayed.

US-004: Chrono-Gunner - Time Stop Interaction

Scenario 1: Player stops time while enemies are active Given there are 3 active enemies and 5 active projectiles on screen When the Chrono-Gunner activates 'Time Stop' Then all 3 enemies and all 5 projectiles should freeze in place for 4 seconds.

Scenario 2: Player stops time while an enemy is firing Given an enemy is in the process of firing a projectile When the Chrono-Gunner activates 'Time Stop' Then the enemy's firing animation should pause, and the projectile should stop mid-air.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Player Data Structure

This specification defines the data structure for storing all information related to a player's profile and current game session.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_id String A unique identifier for the player.
class_id String The ID of the currently selected player class (e.g., 'chrono_soldier').
total_runs_completed Integer The total number of runs the player has finished.
total_time_played Float The total cumulative time the player has spent in the game, in seconds.
unlocked_classes Array of Strings A list of the player's unlocked class IDs.
current_run_data Object Contains all data specific to the current, ongoing run.
current_run_data.start_time Float The Unix timestamp when the current run began.
current_run_data.run_seed Integer The seed used for procedural generation in the current run.
current_run_data.score Integer The player's score for the current run.
current_run_data.level_reached Integer The highest level the player reached in the current run.
current_run_data.chrono_meter_max Float The maximum capacity of the Chrono-Meter for the current run.
current_run_data.chrono_meter_current Float The current charge of the Chrono-Meter for the current run.
current_run_data.rewind_charges_max Integer The maximum number of Rewind charges the player has for the current run.
current_run_data.rewind_charges_current Integer The current number of Rewind charges the player has for the current run.
current_run_data.time_stop_charges_max Integer The maximum number of Time Stop charges the player has for the current run.
current_run_data.time_stop_charges_current Integer The current number of Time Stop charges the player has for the current run.
current_run_data.time_stop_cooldown_end Float The Unix timestamp when the Time Stop ability will be off cooldown.

TS-002: Player Class Data Structure

This specification defines the data structure for each player class.

Field Name Data Type Description
class_id String A unique identifier for the class (e.g., 'chrono_soldier').
name String The display name of the class (e.g., 'Chrono-Soldier').
description String A short description of the class's theme and playstyle.
base_health Float The player's starting health value.
base_speed Float The player's base movement speed.
base_chrono_meter_regen_rate Float The rate at which the Chrono-Meter regenerates per second.
base_rewind_cooldown Float The cooldown time in seconds for the Rewind ability.
base_rewind_duration Float The duration in seconds of the Rewind effect.
base_time_stop_cooldown Float The cooldown time in seconds for the Time Stop ability.
base_time_stop_duration Float The duration in seconds of the Time Stop effect.
base_time_stop_cost Float The amount of Chrono-Meter required to use Time Stop.

TS-005: API Endpoints Specification

This specification outlines the necessary API endpoints for managing game state and data.

Endpoint HTTP Method Description
/game/new_run POST Starts a new game run, generating a seed and initializing player state.
/game/update_state POST Sends the current game state (player position, health, ammo, Chrono-Meter, etc.) to the server for persistence. This should be called frequently.
/game/finalize_run POST Marks the current run as complete, saves the final score and stats, and potentially unlocks new content.
/player/get_profile GET Retrieves the player's profile data, including unlocked classes and total stats.
/player/unlock_class POST Marks a new class as unlocked for the player.
/content/get_weapon_list GET Retrieves the full list of all available weapons.
/content/get_class_list GET Retrieves the full list of all available player classes.

TS-006: Core Gameplay Loop - State Machine

This specification defines the high-level state machine for the main gameplay loop.

State Description
MainMenu The initial state where the player can start a new run, view their profile, or access settings.
InGame The primary gameplay state where the player controls their character, fights enemies, and progresses through levels.
Paused A temporary state where the game is halted, accessible from the 'InGame' state.
GameOver The state reached upon player death, displaying the final score and options to restart or return to the main menu.
LevelComplete A transitional state reached upon clearing a level, displaying stats and offering the option to proceed to the next level.

TS-007: Core Gameplay Loop - Player Actions

This specification details the player's primary actions within the 'InGame' state.

Action Input Description
Move WASD / Left Stick Standard directional movement.
Fire Weapon Left Click / Right Trigger Fires the currently equipped weapon.
Switch Weapon Number Keys / D-Pad Cycles through the player's equipped weapons.
Activate Rewind 'E' Key / Left Bumper Uses a Rewind charge to revert position and health by 5 seconds. Requires a charge and is on cooldown.
Activate Time Stop 'Q' Key / Right Bumper Uses a Time Stop charge to freeze enemies and projectiles for 4 seconds. Requires a charge and is on cooldown.
Interact 'F' Key / 'A' Button Interacts with objects in the environment (e.g., picking up items).

Initial Weapon Set (Chrono-Pistol, Plasma Rifle, Laser SMG, Time Grenade)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player Fires Chrono-Pistol Given the player has the Chrono-Pistol equipped and has ammo When they press the fire button Then a single shot is fired, ammo is consumed, and a bullet is launched forward.

US-002: Player Fires Plasma Rifle Given the player has the Plasma Rifle equipped and has ammo When they hold down the fire button Then multiple shots are fired in quick succession, ammo is consumed for each shot, and multiple projectiles are launched.

US-003: Player Uses Time Grenade Given the player has a Time Grenade in their inventory When they throw the Time Grenade Then the grenade travels forward and explodes on impact or after a set time, creating a localized time-slowing field.

{ "content": "# Chrono-Bullet Hell: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Technical Specifications\n\n## TS-001: Player State & Core Data Structures\n\n### 1. Player Data Structure\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| playerID | String | Unique identifier for the player. |\n| currentClassID | String | The ID of the player's currently selected class. |\n| maxHealth | Integer | The maximum health value for the player. |\n| currentHealth | Integer | The player's current health value. |\n| chronoMeterMax | Integer | The maximum capacity of the Chrono-Meter. |\n| chronoMeterCurrent | Integer | The current amount of Chrono-Meter energy. |\n| inventory | Array of Strings | A list of the IDs of all weapons the player is carrying. |\n| equippedWeaponID | String | The ID of the weapon the player currently has equipped. |\n| metaProgressionFlags | Object | A collection of flags to track unlocked content (e.g., { "class_Chrono_Gunner": true }). |\n\n### 2. Class Data Structure\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| classID | String | Unique identifier for the class (e.g., "Chrono_Soldier"). |\n| displayName | String | The user-facing name of the class. |\n| description | String | A short description of the class's playstyle. |\n| startingHealth | Integer | The base maximum health for this class. |\n| startingChronoMeterMax | Integer | The base maximum Chrono-Meter capacity for this class. |\n| startingInventory | Array of Strings | A list of weapon IDs the player starts with. |\n\n### 3. Weapon Data Structure\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| weaponID | String | Unique identifier for the weapon (e.g., "Chrono_Pistol"). |\n| displayName | String | The user-facing name of the weapon. |\n| description | String | A short description of the weapon's function. |\n| weaponType | String | The type of weapon (e.g., "Pistol", "Rifle", "Grenade"). |\n| ammoType | String | The type of ammo required (e.g., "Bullet", "Energy"). |\n| maxAmmoCarried | Integer | The maximum number of shots the player can carry for this ammo type. |\n| baseDamage | Float | The base damage dealt per shot/projectile. |\n| fireRate | Float | The time in seconds between shots. |\n| projectileSpeed | Float | The speed at which the projectile travels. |\n| ammoCostPerShot | Integer | The amount of ammo consumed per shot. |\n\n### 4. Game State Data Structure\n\n| Field Name | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| runID | String | Unique identifier for the current run. |\n| playerState | Player Data Structure | The complete state of the player at the start of the run. |\n| currentLevelSeed | String | The seed used to generate the current level. |\n| currentLevelIndex | Integer | The index of the current level in the run. |\n\n## TS-002: Core Gameplay Systems - Time Manipulation\n\n### 1. Rewind Mechanic\n\n* Functionality: Allows the player to reverse their own position and the state of nearby objects for a short duration. This is the core mechanic of the 'Chrono-Soldier' class.

  • Data:
    • Rewind Duration: 5 seconds (configurable).
    • Chrono-Meter Cost: 100 Chrono-Meter energy per second of rewind.
    • State Buffer: A data structure that stores the player's position, rotation, health, and ammo for the last 5 seconds.
  • Logic:
    1. When the player activates Rewind, the game checks if they have enough Chrono-Meter energy.
    2. If sufficient, the player's state is set to what it was 1 second prior.
    3. The Chrono-Meter is drained at the specified rate.
    4. The state buffer is updated.
    5. The player is made temporarily invulnerable during the rewind to prevent damage exploitation.

2. Timeline Leaping (Chrono-Gunner Ability)

  • Functionality: Allows the player to instantly travel forward in time to a designated point, bypassing immediate threats. This is the core mechanic of the 'Chrono-Gunner' class.
  • Data:
    • Leap Distance: 15 meters (configurable).
    • Chrono-Meter Cost: 75 Chrono-Meter energy.
    • Cooldown: 8 seconds.
  • Logic:
    1. The player aims at a valid location within the Leap Distance.
    2. Upon activation, the player's state is instantly updated to the new location.
    3. The Chrono-Meter is debited.
    4. The ability enters its cooldown period.
    5. The player is briefly invulnerable after the leap.

3. Chrono-Meter System\n\n* Functionality: The central resource for all time-based abilities.

  • Data:
    • Max Capacity: 200 Chrono-Meter energy (base, modified by class).
    • Regeneration Rate: 5 Chrono-Meter energy per second.
    • Regeneration Condition: Chrono-Meter only regenerates when the player is not taking damage.
  • Logic:
    1. The game constantly checks for incoming player damage.
    2. If damage is taken, regeneration is paused.
    3. If no damage is taken for 1 second, regeneration begins.
    4. The meter increases at the specified rate until it reaches its maximum capacity.

4. Temporal Entropy System (Basic)\n\n* Functionality: A global difficulty scaling mechanic that introduces negative temporal effects as the player progresses through a run.

  • Data:
    • Effect Trigger Thresholds: The game will trigger a random negative effect at specific level indices (e.g., Level 3, Level 6).
    • Time Grenade (Example): The Time Grenade's area of effect and duration may increase with Temporal Entropy.
  • Logic:
    1. At the start of each new level, the game checks if the current level index meets an Entropy trigger threshold.
    2. If it does, a random negative effect from a predefined list is applied to the player for the remainder of the run.

TS-003: Weapon & Combat Logic\n\n### 1. Chrono-Pistol\n\n* Data: Damage: 15, Fire Rate: 0.5s, Ammo Cost: 1, Projectile Speed: 30 m/s, Ammo Type: Bullet.

  • Logic: Fires a single, fast-moving bullet on each button press. Consumes 1 bullet and 1 Chrono-Meter energy per shot.

2. Plasma Rifle\n\n* Data: Damage: 12, Fire Rate: 0.1s, Ammo Cost: 1, Projectile Speed: 40 m/s, Ammo Type: Energy.

  • Logic: Fires a rapid burst of plasma shots while the button is held. Consumes 1 bullet and 1 Chrono-Meter energy per shot.

3. Laser SMG\n\n* Data: Damage: 8, Fire Rate: 0.05s, Ammo Cost: 1, Projectile Speed: 50 m/s, Ammo Type: Energy.

  • Logic: Fires a continuous beam of laser shots while the button is held. Consumes 1 bullet and 1 Chrono-Meter energy per shot.

4. Time Grenade\n\n* Data: Damage: 50, Explosion Radius: 8m, Duration: 4s, Ammo Cost: 25 Chrono-Meter energy, Travel Speed: 15 m/s.

  • Logic: A thrown projectile that explodes on impact or after 4 seconds. The explosion creates a localized field that slows all enemies within its radius by 50%. Consumes 25 Chrono-Meter energy.

TS-004: Procedural Generation & Level Design\n\n### 1. Level Generation\n\n* Algorithm: Seed-based procedural generation using a cellular automata or similar approach.

  • Input: A unique string seed.
  • Output: A 2D tilemap representing the level layout.
  • Features: The generator must be able to create varied, non-linear layouts with chokepoints, open arenas, and verticality.

2. Level Structure\n\n* Progression: The game will consist of a series of levels (e.g., 10 levels).

  • End Condition: The player must defeat a boss at the final level to win the run.
  • Replayability: Each new run will use a different seed to generate a unique level layout.

TS-005: API Endpoints (Server-Side / State Management)\n\n### 1. POST /new_run\n\n* Description: Starts a new game run.

  • Request Body: { "playerClassID": "Chrono_Soldier", "seed": "..." }
  • Response Body: { "runID": "...", "initialState": { ... } }

2. POST /update_state\n\n* Description: Sends the player's actions and receives the updated game state. This is the primary endpoint during a run.

  • Request Body: { "runID": "...", "playerInput": { "move": [x, y], "fire": true, "useAbility": "..." }, "currentLevelSeed": "..." }
  • Response Body: { "nextState": { ... }, "levelTransition": false }

3. POST /finalize_run\n\n* Description: Ends the game run (win or lose).

  • Request Body: { "runID": "...", "outcome": "win/lose", "totalTime": 120, "levelsCompleted": 10 }
  • Response Body: { "metaProgressionUnlocked": [ ... ] }" }

Seed-Based Procedural Generation (US-004)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-004: Seed-Based Procedural Generation

Scenario 1: Generating a new level with a specific seed

Given the player has not yet generated a level When the player enters a specific seed (e.g., "12345") and initiates level generation Then a new, procedurally generated level is created and loaded into the game And the seed used for generation is stored and displayed to the player.

Scenario 2: Replaying a level with the same seed

Given the player has previously generated a level with a specific seed (e.g., "12345") When the player enters the same seed again and initiates level generation Then the exact same level layout, enemy placement, and power-up locations as the first generation are recreated.

Scenario 3: Generating a new level with a random seed

Given the player is on the level generation screen When the player selects the option to generate a level with a random seed Then a new, procedurally generated level is created and loaded And a unique, random seed is automatically assigned and displayed to the player.

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Unlock 'The Chronomancer'

Scenario 1: Player unlocks the Chronomancer by completing the first boss. Given the player has not yet unlocked 'The Chronomancer' and has completed the 'Temporal Guardian' boss. When the game saves the player's progress after the 'Temporal Guardian' is defeated. Then 'The Chronomancer' should be available for selection in the character menu.

Scenario 2: Player cannot select an un-unlocked character. Given the player has not yet unlocked 'The Chronomancer'. When the player attempts to select 'The Chronomancer' from the character menu. Then the game should display a message indicating that the character is locked and show the required completion criteria.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Player Data Structure

This specification defines the data structure for storing all persistent player information.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_id String A unique identifier for the player.
player_name String The player's chosen name.
unlocked_classes Array of Strings A list of the IDs of all player classes that the player has unlocked.
current_class_id String The ID of the player class that is currently selected.
currency_meta Integer The amount of meta-currency the player has earned.
run_history Array of Objects A log of past runs, containing details like completion time, score, and classes used.

TS-002: Player Class Data Structure

This specification defines the data structure for each player class.

Field Name Data Type Description
class_id String A unique identifier for the class (e.g., 'chrono_soldier').
display_name String The name of the class as shown to the player.
description String A short bio for the class.
unlock_criteria String A description of the condition required to unlock this class.
base_stats Object The starting stats for the class.
base_stats.health Float The base health value.
base_stats.chrono_meter_capacity Float The base capacity of the Chrono-Meter.
base_stats.chrono_meter_regen_rate Float The base regeneration rate of the Chrono-Meter per second.
starting_weapon_id String The ID of the weapon the player begins with.
starting_abilities Array of Strings A list of the IDs of the special abilities the player starts with.

TS-003: Weapon Data Structure

This specification defines the data structure for all player weapons.

Field Name Data Type Description
weapon_id String A unique identifier for the weapon (e.g., 'chrono_pistol').
display_name String The name of the weapon.
description String A short description of the weapon.
weapon_type String The type of weapon (e.g., 'pistol', 'rifle').
damage Float The base damage per shot.
fire_rate Float The time between shots in seconds.
ammo_capacity Integer The maximum number of shots the weapon can hold.
projectile_speed Float The speed at which the projectile travels.
special_properties Object A container for unique weapon effects.
special_properties.is_time_based Boolean True if the weapon has time-based effects.
special_properties.time_cost Float The amount of Chrono-Meter consumed per shot, if applicable.

TS-004: Ability Data Structure

This specification defines the data structure for all player abilities.

Field Name Data Type Description
ability_id String A unique identifier for the ability (e.g., 'rewind').
display_name String The name of the ability.
description String A short description of the ability's function.
cooldown Float The time in seconds before the ability can be used again.
chrono_meter_cost Float The amount of Chrono-Meter required to activate the ability.
effect_type String The type of effect the ability has (e.g., 'rewind', 'dash').
effect_parameters Object A container for the specific data related to the effect.
effect_parameters.rewind_duration Float The duration of the rewind in seconds.

TS-005: Game State Data Structure

This specification defines the data structure for the player's current game session.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_stats Object The player's current stats for this run.
player_stats.health Float The player's current health.
player_stats.chrono_meter_value Float The player's current Chrono-Meter charge.
player_stats.current_weapon_id String The ID of the weapon the player is currently holding.
player_stats.current_abilities Array of Strings The IDs of the abilities the player has access to in this run.
current_level_id String The ID of the current level being played.
procedural_seed Integer The seed used to generate the current level.

TS-006: API Endpoint: Start New Run

This specification defines the API endpoint for initiating a new game run.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_id String The ID of the player starting the run.
class_id String The ID of the player class to use for this run.
starting_weapon_id String The ID of the weapon the player will start with.
starting_abilities Array of Strings The IDs of the abilities the player will start with.
procedural_seed Integer The seed for level generation.

TS-007: API Endpoint: Update Game State

This specification defines the API endpoint for saving the player's progress during a run.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_id String The ID of the player.
game_state Object The complete current game state object (as defined in TS-005).

TS-008: API Endpoint: Finalize Run

This specification defines the API endpoint for ending a game run.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_id String The ID of the player.
final_score Integer The player's final score for the run.
completion_time_seconds Float The total duration of the run in seconds.
classes_used Array of Strings The IDs of all player classes encountered during the run.
weapons_found Array of Strings The IDs of all weapons collected during the run.
new_unlocks Array of Strings The IDs of any new classes or items unlocked during the run.

TS-018: Player Stats Progression (Initial Logic)

player_stats.chrono_meter_regen_rate Float The player's current Chrono-Meter regeneration rate. This value is based on the selected class's base rate and any upgrades.
