User Stories & Criteria

US-001 Scenario 1: Player successfully selects the 'Bullet' class Given the player is on the class selection screen When they select the 'Bullet' class and confirm their choice Then the player's active class is set to 'Bullet' and the game begins.

US-002 Scenario 2: Player successfully selects the 'Time' class Given the player is on the class selection screen When they select the 'Time' class and confirm their choice Then the player's active class is set to 'Time' and the game begins.

US-003 Scenario 3: Player successfully selects the 'Gravity' class Given the player is on the class selection screen When they select the 'Gravity' class and confirm their choice Then the player's active class is set to 'Gravity' and the game begins.

US-004 Scenario 4: Player successfully selects the 'Energy' class Given the player is on the class selection screen When they select the 'Energy' class and confirm their choice Then the player's active class is set to 'Energy' and the game begins.

US-005 Scenario 5: Player successfully equips the 'Plasma Rifle' Given the player is the 'Bullet' class and has the 'Plasma Rifle' in their inventory When they equip the 'Plasma Rifle' Then the player's active weapon is the 'Plasma Rifle' and their stats reflect the 'Bullet' class.

US-006 Scenario 6: Player successfully equips the 'Time Manipulator' Given the player is the 'Time' class and has the 'Time Manipulator' in their inventory When they equip the 'Time Manipulator' Then the player's active weapon is the 'Time Manipulator' and their stats reflect the 'Time' class.

US-007 Scenario 7: Player successfully equips the 'Gravity Gun' Given the player is the 'Gravity' class and has the 'Gravity Gun' in their inventory When they equip the 'Gravity Gun' Then the player's active weapon is the 'Gravity Gun' and their stats reflect the 'Gravity' class.

US-008 Scenario 8: Player successfully equips the 'Laser Cannon' Given the player is the 'Energy' class and has the 'Laser Cannon' in their inventory When they equip the 'Laser Cannon' Then the player's active weapon is the 'Laser Cannon' and their stats reflect the 'Energy' class.

US-009 Scenario 9: Player successfully upgrades the 'Plasma Rifle' Given the player has the 'Plasma Rifle' and enough upgrade points When they spend the points to upgrade the 'Plasma Rifle' Then the 'Plasma Rifle' in their inventory has increased damage and rate of fire.

US-010 Scenario 10: Player successfully upgrades the 'Time Manipulator' Given the player has the 'Time Manipulator' and enough upgrade points When they spend the points to upgrade the 'Time Manipulator' Then the 'Time Manipulator' in their inventory has increased rewind duration and reduced cooldown.

Technical Specifications

Chrono-Bullet Hell: Technical Specifications

TS-001: Player Data Structure

This defines the data that must be stored for each player profile.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_id String A unique identifier for the player.
username String The player's display name.
active_class String The ID of the currently selected player class. Must match a key in the PlayerClasses table.
unlocked_classes Array of Strings A list of all player classes the player has unlocked.
inventory Object A collection of the player's owned weapons and items. The structure will be defined in TS-003.
meta_progression_points Integer Points earned that can be spent on unlocking new classes. Must be non-negative.

TS-002: Player Class Data Structure

This defines the data for each unique player class.

Field Name Data Type Description
class_id String A unique identifier for the class (e.g., "Chrono-Soldier").
display_name String The name of the class as shown to the player.
description String A short description of the class's lore and playstyle.
base_stats Object The core, unmodded stats for this class.
base_stats.health Float The player's base maximum health. Must be positive.
base_stats.move_speed Float The player's base movement speed. Must be positive.
base_stats.chrono_meter_capacity Float The maximum amount of Chrono-Meter the player can hold. Must be positive.
base_stats.chrono_meter_regen_rate Float The rate at which the Chrono-Meter regenerates per second. Must be non-negative.
starting_weapon_id String The ID of the weapon the player begins with. Must match a key in the Weapons table.
unlock_cost Integer The number of meta-progression points required to unlock this class. Must be non-negative.

TS-003: Weapon Data Structure

This defines the data for each weapon in the game.

Field Name Data Type Description
weapon_id String A unique identifier for the weapon (e.g., "PlasmaRifle").
display_name String The name of the weapon.
description String A short description of the weapon.
class_compatibility Array of Strings A list of class IDs that can equip this weapon.
base_stats Object The base, unupgraded stats for this weapon.
base_stats.damage Float The base damage per hit. Must be positive.
base_stats.rate_of_fire Float The time in seconds between shots. Must be positive.
base_stats.ammo_capacity Integer The maximum number of shots the weapon can hold. Must be positive.
base_stats.ammo_per_shot Integer The amount of ammo consumed per shot. Must be positive.
base_stats.rewind_cost Float The amount of Chrono-Meter required to use the weapon's special ability (if any). Must be non-negative.
base_stats.rewind_duration Float The duration of the special ability's effect. Must be non-negative.
upgrade_path Object Defines the upgrade tree for this weapon.
upgrade_path.max_level Integer The total number of upgrade levels. Must be positive.
upgrade_path.levels Array of Objects A list defining the stats at each upgrade level.
upgrade_path.levels[i].level Integer The upgrade level (1 to max_level).
upgrade_path.levels[i].cost Integer The meta-progression points required to reach this level. Must be non-negative.
upgrade_path.levels[i].damage_multiplier Float The multiplier applied to the base damage at this level. Must be >= 1.0.
upgrade_path.levels[i].rate_of_fire_multiplier Float The multiplier applied to the base rate of fire at this level. Must be <= 1.0.
upgrade_path.levels[i].rewind_duration_multiplier Float The multiplier applied to the base rewind duration at this level. Must be >= 1.0.

TS-004: Game State Data Structure

This defines the data that must be saved and loaded for the game's state.

Field Name Data Type Description
player_data Object The player's profile data, as defined in TS-001.
current_run_data Object Data specific to the current roguelike run.
current_run_data.seed Integer The seed used for procedural generation in this run.
current_run_data.level_seed Integer The seed used for level generation in this run.
current_run_data.player_class String The class ID selected for this run. Must match a key in PlayerClasses.
current_run_data.player_stats Object The player's stats for this run, including base stats and any modifiers from weapons or upgrades.
current_run_data.player_stats.health Float Current health. Must be between 0 and max health.
current_run_data.player_stats.move_speed Float Current movement speed. Must be positive.
current_run_data.player_stats.chrono_meter_capacity Float Current Chrono-Meter capacity. Must be positive.
current_run_data.player_stats.chrono_meter_regen_rate Float Current Chrono-Meter regeneration rate. Must be non-negative.
current_run_data.player_stats.chrono_meter_current Float The current amount of Chrono-Meter. Must be between 0 and capacity.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon Object The data for the currently equipped weapon. This should be a copy of the weapon data from the player's inventory, including its current upgrade level and stats.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.damage Float Current damage. Must be positive.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rate_of_fire Float Current rate of fire. Must be positive.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.ammo_capacity Integer Current ammo capacity. Must be positive.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.ammo_per_shot Integer Current ammo per shot. Must be positive.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rewind_cost Float Current rewind cost. Must be non-negative.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rewind_duration Float Current rewind duration. Must be non-negative.
current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.upgrade_level Integer The current upgrade level of the equipped weapon. Must be between 0 and max_level.
current_run_data.player_stats.inventory Array of Weapon IDs A list of all weapon IDs the player has access to in this run. This should be derived from the player's unlocked classes and any weapons found.
current_run_data.temporal_entropy Float The current level of temporal entropy for this run. Must be non-negative.

TS-005: API Endpoints

This defines the core API endpoints required to manage player data and runs.

Endpoint Method Description
/player/profile GET Retrieves the player's profile data (username, unlocked classes, etc.).
/player/profile PUT Updates the player's profile data (e.g., changes active class).
/run/new POST Starts a new roguelike run. Requires the class_id and seed as input. Returns the initial current_run_data.
/run/update PUT Updates the state of the current run (e.g., player position, health, Chrono-Meter, inventory changes). Requires the full current_run_data.
/run/finalize POST Ends the current run. Requires the final current_run_data to process meta-progression rewards.

TS-006: User Stories (Refactored)

This section refactors the provided user stories into a more structured format, focusing on the technical acceptance criteria for each feature.

US-001: Select Player Class

Given a player has unlocked the 'Bullet' class: When they select 'Bullet' on the class selection screen and confirm Then the player_data.active_class in the API is updated to 'Bullet'. And the current_run_data.player_class is set to 'Bullet'. And the current_run_data.player_stats are populated with the base_stats from the 'Bullet' class definition. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is set to the 'Chrono-Pistol' (the starting weapon for 'Bullet').

US-002: Select Player Class

Given a player has unlocked the 'Time' class: When they select 'Time' on the class selection screen and confirm Then the player_data.active_class in the API is updated to 'Time'. And the current_run_data.player_class is set to 'Time'. And the current_run_data.player_stats are populated with the base_stats from the 'Time' class definition. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is set to the 'Time Grenade' (the starting weapon for 'Time').

US-003: Select Player Class

Given a player has unlocked the 'Gravity' class: When they select 'Gravity' on the class selection screen and confirm Then the player_data.active_class in the API is updated to 'Gravity'. And the current_run_data.player_class is set to 'Gravity'. And the current_run_data.player_stats are populated with the base_stats from the 'Gravity' class definition. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is set to the 'Gravity Gun' (the starting weapon for 'Gravity').

US-004: Select Player Class

Given a player has unlocked the 'Energy' class: When they select 'Energy' on the class selection screen and confirm Then the player_data.active_class in the API is updated to 'Energy'. And the current_run_data.player_class is set to 'Energy'. And the current_run_data.player_stats are populated with the base_stats from the 'Energy' class definition. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is set to the 'Laser SMG' (the starting weapon for 'Energy').

US-005: Equip Weapon

Given the player is the 'Bullet' class and has the 'Plasma Rifle' equipped: When they equip the 'Plasma Rifle' from their inventory Then the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is updated to the 'Plasma Rifle' data. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.upgrade_level is set to 0. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.damage is set to the base_stats.damage of the 'Plasma Rifle'. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rate_of_fire is set to the base_stats.rate_of_fire of the 'Plasma Rifle'.

US-006: Equip Weapon

Given the player is the 'Time' class and has the 'Time Manipulator' equipped: When they equip the 'Time Manipulator' from their inventory Then the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is updated to the 'Time Manipulator' data. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.upgrade_level is set to 0. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rewind_duration is set to the base_stats.rewind_duration of the 'Time Manipulator'. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rewind_cost is set to the base_stats.rewind_cost of the 'Time Manipulator'.

US-007: Equip Weapon

Given the player is the 'Gravity' class and has the 'Gravity Gun' equipped: When they equip the 'Gravity Gun' from their inventory Then the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is updated to the 'Gravity Gun' data. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.upgrade_level is set to 0. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.damage is set to the base_stats.damage of the 'Gravity Gun'. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rewind_cost is set to the base_stats.rewind_cost of the 'Gravity Gun'.

US-008: Equip Weapon

Given the player is the 'Energy' class and has the 'Laser Cannon' equipped: When they equip the 'Laser Cannon' from their inventory Then the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon is updated to the 'Laser Cannon' data. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.upgrade_level is set to 0. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.damage is set to the base_stats.damage of the 'Laser Cannon'. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rate_of_fire is set to the base_stats.rate_of_fire of the 'Laser Cannon'.

US-009: Upgrade Weapon

Given the player is the 'Bullet' class and has the 'Plasma Rifle' equipped with upgrade_level = 1: When they spend the required meta-progression points to upgrade to level 2 Then the player_data.meta_progression_points is reduced by the upgrade_path.levels[1].cost. And the player_data.unlocked_classes is updated to include the 'Bullet' class if it wasn't already. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.upgrade_level is updated to 2. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.damage is updated to reflect the upgrade_path.levels[2].damage_multiplier applied to the base damage.

US-010: Upgrade Weapon

Given the player is the 'Time' class and has the 'Time Manipulator' equipped with upgrade_level = 2: When they spend the required meta-progression points to upgrade to level 3 Then the player_data.meta_progression_points is reduced by the upgrade_path.levels[2].cost. And the player_data.unlocked_classes is updated to include the 'Time' class if it wasn't already. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.upgrade_level is updated to 3. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rewind_duration is updated to reflect the upgrade_path.levels[3].rewind_duration_multiplier applied to the base duration. And the current_run_data.player_stats.weapon.rewind_cost is updated to reflect the new duration (if the system is designed that way).

Essential API Endpoints (New Run, Update State, Finalize Run)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player initiates a new run Given the player is on the main menu When they select the 'Start New Run' option Then a new game session is created, and the player is placed in the first level.

US-002: Player successfully rewinds time Given the player has taken damage in the current run When they activate the 'Rewind' ability Then their health is restored to the value it was 5 seconds prior.

US-003: Player completes a run Given the player has defeated the final boss When the victory screen is displayed Then the run data is saved to their profile, and they are returned to the main menu.

Technical Specifications

Chrono-Bullet Hell: Minimum Viable Product (MVP) Technical Specifications

1. User Story Refactoring

US-001: Player initiates a new run

Given the player is on the main menu When they select the 'Start New Run' option Then a new game session is created, and the player is placed in the first level.

US-002: Player successfully rewinds time

Given the player has taken damage in the current run When they activate the 'Rewind' ability Then their health is restored to the value it was 5 seconds prior.

US-003: Player completes a run

Given the player has defeated the final boss When the victory screen is displayed Then the run data is saved to their profile, and they are returned to the main menu.

2. MVP Feature Breakdown & Technical Specifications

TS-001: Core Gameplay Loop & State Management

Description: This specification covers the fundamental systems that drive the roguelike experience, including player state, run data, and the core game loop.

Field Name Type Description
playerState Object Contains the current state of the player within a run.
playerState.health Float The player's current health points.
playerState.maxHealth Float The player's maximum health, potentially modified by upgrades.
playerState.chronoMeter Float The current charge of the player's time abilities.
playerState.maxChronoMeter Float The maximum charge capacity of the Chrono-Meter.
playerState.currentWeapon String The name or ID of the weapon the player is currently holding.
playerState.inventory Array A list of the player's currently held weapons and items.
playerState.runSeed String A unique seed used to procedurally generate the current run.
playerState.level Integer The current level number the player is in.
playerState.runStartTime Timestamp The date and time when the current run began.
playerState.runEndTime Timestamp The date and time when the current run ended (null if ongoing).
playerState.runDuration Integer The total time in seconds the current run has lasted.
playerState.runOutcome String The result of the run ('Victory', 'Defeat', 'Quit').
playerState.runScore Integer The final score achieved at the end of the run.
playerState.class String The name or ID of the player's chosen class.
playerState.metaProgress Object A container for all persistent player unlocks and upgrades.
playerState.metaProgress.unlockedClasses Array A list of the names or IDs of all classes the player has unlocked.
playerState.metaProgress.unlockedWeapons Array A list of the names or IDs of all weapons the player has unlocked.

TS-002: Player Movement & Combat

Description: Defines the core player actions and their associated data.

Field Name Type Description
playerInput Object Contains the current state of player inputs.
playerInput.moveX Float The horizontal movement input (-1.0 to 1.0).
playerInput.moveY Float The vertical movement input (-1.0 to 1.0).
playerInput.aimX Float The horizontal aim direction (-1.0 to 1.0).
playerInput.aimY Float The vertical aim direction (-1.0 to 1.0).
playerInput.fire Boolean True if the player is holding down the fire button.
playerInput.rewind Boolean True if the player is holding down the rewind button.

User Stories & Criteria

US-001: Player Rewind

Scenario 1: Player successfully rewinds time Given the player has 3 'Rewind' charges and has just taken damage When the player activates the Rewind ability Then the player's health should be restored to its previous state, and one charge should be consumed.

Scenario 2: Player attempts to rewind with no charges Given the player has 0 'Rewind' charges When the player attempts to activate the Rewind ability Then the ability should be unresponsive, and no visual or audio feedback should occur.

Scenario 3: Player rewinds into an obstacle Given the player is standing next to a wall and has a Rewind charge When the player activates Rewind and the effect would move them into the wall Then the player should be stopped at the wall's collision boundary, and the charge should not be consumed.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Player Rewind System

1. Overview

This system allows the player to reverse their own position and state by a short duration, consuming a limited resource.

2. Core Logic

  • The system records the player's state (position, health, ammo, etc.) at regular intervals (e.g., every 0.1 seconds).
  • Upon activation, the game rewinds the player's state to a point in the past (e.g., 3 seconds ago).
  • The player's Chrono-Meter is immediately debited.
  • The player cannot rewind if their Chrono-Meter is empty.
  • The player cannot rewind if the resulting position would be inside a solid object.

3. Data Structure

Field Name Type Description
maxCharges integer The maximum number of Rewind charges the player can hold.
currentCharges integer The number of Rewind charges the player currently possesses.
rewindDuration float The duration in seconds that the player is rewound. (e.g., 3.0)
chargeRegenRate float The rate at which charges regenerate per second. (e.g., 0.1)
chargeRegenDelay float The delay in seconds after taking damage before charge regeneration begins. (e.g., 5.0)
stateHistorySize integer The number of past states to store for rewinding. (e.g., 300 for 3 seconds at 0.1s intervals)

4. System Dependencies

  • Player State Manager
  • Chrono-Meter System
  • Collision System

Chrono-Meter Regeneration (US-005)

▼

User Stories & Criteria

US-005: Chrono-Meter Regeneration

Scenario 1: Chrono-Meter regenerates at base rate

Given the player's Chrono-Meter is at 50% full When 10 seconds of gameplay pass without the player using any abilities Then the Chrono-Meter should be at 60% full (assuming a 1% per second regeneration rate).

Scenario 2: Chrono-Meter does not regenerate while in a time-slow bubble

Given the player is inside a time-slow bubble they created And their Chrono-Meter is at 75% full When 5 seconds of gameplay pass Then the Chrono-Meter should remain at 75% full.

Scenario 3: Chrono-Meter does not regenerate when dead

Given the player character is dead When the respawn timer is active Then the Chrono-Meter should remain at 0% full.

Technical Specifications

TS-001: Chrono-Meter System

1. Overview

This document defines the core data structure and logic for the Chrono-Meter, the primary resource for all player abilities.

2. Data Structure

Field Name Type Description
maxCapacity float The total capacity of the Chrono-Meter (e.g., 100.0).
currentCharge float The current amount of charge in the Chrono-Meter.
regenerationRate float The rate at which the Chrono-Meter regenerates per second when the player is alive and not in a slow-time field.
isRegenerating bool A flag indicating if the meter is currently regenerating.
lastAbilityCost float The amount of charge consumed by the last used ability. Used for cooldown logic.
lastAbilityTime float The game timestamp when the last ability was used. Used for cooldown calculations.
cooldownDuration float The duration of the cooldown for the last used ability.

3. Core Logic

  1. Regeneration: The isRegenerating flag is set to true if the player is alive and not inside a slow-time field. If isRegenerating is true, currentCharge is incremented by regenerationRate * deltaTime. The charge cannot exceed maxCapacity.
  2. Ability Use: When an ability is used, its specified charge cost is deducted from currentCharge. If currentCharge is less than the cost, the ability cannot be used. The lastAbilityCost and lastAbilityTime are updated, and the isRegenerating flag is temporarily set to false to initiate a short cooldown before regeneration resumes.

Technical Design Document (TDD)

▼

1.0 Introduction

▼

1.0 Introduction\n\n## 1.1 Purpose\nThis Technical Design Document (TDD) serves as the authoritative reference for the development and implementation of 'Chrono-Bullet Hell.' It outlines the architecture, data models, and logic flows required to deliver a high-performance roguelike experience featuring multi-dimensional time manipulation and deterministic procedural generation.\n\n## 1.2 Scope\nThe scope of this document covers the core gameplay systems (movement, combat, temporal mechanics), the backend API integration for run validation and meta-progression, and the data structures necessary for state persistence and replayability.\n\n## 1.3 Objectives\n* Implement a performant snapshot-based circular buffer for time manipulation.\n* Ensure deterministic run generation using seed-based procedural logic.\n* Integrate a robust API for state reconciliation and persistent meta-progression.\n* Define clear class and weapon matrices for balanced gameplay.

2.0 System Architecture

▼

2.0 System Architecture\n\n## 2.1 Overview\nChrono-Bullet Hell utilizes a client-authoritative model with server-side validation. The core engine manages a high-frequency Chrono-Clock for temporal mechanics, while the backend handles persistence and seed-based run initialization.\n\n## 2.2 Technology Stack\n* Client Engine: Unity/C# (Implied by physics and vector handling).\n* State Management: Snapshot-based Circular Buffer (60ms frequency).\n* Backend: RESTful API (Node.js/Go/Python) with a relational database for persistence.\n* Communication: JSON-based payloads for state updates and run finalization.\n\n## 2.3 Temporal State Management\nThe game records snapshots of the global state every 2–5 ticks (approx. 60ms). This buffer maintains a rolling 4–5 second history of player transforms, projectile vectors, enemy health, and RNG seeds. Rewinding rolls back the global Chrono-Clock, resetting bullets based on the deterministic seed rather than tracking every coordinate pair.

4.0 API Specification

4.0 API Specification\n\n| Route | Method | Request Body | Success Response | Description |\n| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |\n| /api/v1/new_run | POST | {player_class_id, run_seed?} | {run_id, player_state, level_data} | Initializes a new run with deterministic seed. |\n| /api/v1/update_state | PUT | {run_id, player_input, player_state} | {status, level_update, enemy_updates} | Periodic heartbeat to validate and sync game state. |\n| /api/v1/finalize_run | POST | {run_id, outcome, rooms_cleared, time_elapsed} | {meta_progression_update, unlocks} | Ends run and updates persistent player profile. |\n| /api/player/{id} | GET | None | {player_profile, unlocked_content} | Fetches meta-progression and stats. |\n| /player/unlock_class | POST | {class_id} | {success, updated_unlocked_classes} | Unlocks a new class using meta-currency. |

5.0 Core Feature Implementation

▼

5.0 Core Feature Implementation\n\n## 5.1 Temporal Mechanics\n### US-001: Rewind Mechanic\n* Logic: Upon activation, the system queries the Circular Buffer for the state at T - 3.0s.\n* State Restoration: Reverts position, health, and ammo.\n* Cost: 25% Chrono-Meter (or 40 units per TS-009-B).\n* Constraint: Requires at least 1 'Time Charge' or sufficient meter.\n\n### US-002: Timeline Leaping\n* Logic: Swaps environment assets and enemy spawns between 'Timeline A' and 'Timeline B'.\n* Execution: Maintains player screen coordinates but updates collision layers and active AI entities.\n* Cooldown: 5 seconds.\n\n## 5.2 Resource Systems\n### TS-005: Chrono-Meter System\n* Regeneration: +1.5 units/sec when idle. Paused during firing or ability use.\n* Graze Mechanic: Entering projectile 'Graze' radius without collision grants +2% meter.\n\n### TS-006: Temporal Entropy System\n* Gain: +5% per enemy kill. Increases on damage taken and weapon fire.\n* Thresholds:\n * 26-50%: Minor visual distortion, increased aggression.\n * 76-99%: Random events, reduced regeneration.\n * 100%: Timeline Collapse (Game Over).\n\n## 5.3 Procedural Generation\n### US-004: Seed-Based Generation\n* Algorithm: Uses deterministic noise and pathfinding (A*) governed by run_seed.\n* Components: Room templates, connection maps, and enemy spawn pools are selected based on the seed to ensure identical layouts for identical seeds.\n\n## 5.4 Class-Specific Abilities\n* Chrono-Soldier: Time Stop (5s pause, 60s cooldown), Rewind.\n* Chrono-Gunner: Rapid Fire (2x rate, 8s duration), Time Distortion Field (50% slow AoE).

6.0 Security & Performance

▼

6.0 Security & Performance\n\n## 6.1 Deterministic Validation\nTo prevent cheating, the server uses the run_seed and event_log from update_state to verify that player health and room clears are mathematically possible within the simulation parameters.\n\n## 6.2 Performance Optimization\n* Circular Buffer: Pre-allocated memory to avoid Garbage Collection spikes during high-intensity bullet hell sequences.\n* Projectile Pooling: Bullets are recycled in memory to maintain 60 FPS under high density (1000+ active projectiles).

7.0 Deployment & Operations

▼

7.0 Deployment & Operations\n\n## 7.1 Infrastructure\n* Database: PostgreSQL for structured player and run data.\n* Caching: Redis for active session state to ensure low-latency API responses for update_state calls.\n\n## 7.2 Deployment Pipeline\n* CI/CD: Automated builds for client (Unity Cloud Build) and backend (GitHub Actions to AWS/GCP).\n* Versioning: API versioning (/v1/) to ensure backward compatibility for players on older client versions.

Scope Critique

▼

Multi-Dimensional Time Manipulation

Severity: High

Critique: The GDD lists four distinct time powers but does not provide specific details on their cooldowns, energy costs, or how they interact with each other. The 'Chrono-Meter' is mentioned as the energy source, but the exact cost for each ability is not specified. The 'Temporal Entropy' system is a good idea for balancing, but its specific thresholds and the exact buffs it applies are not detailed.

Suggestion: For each of the four time powers (Rewind, Slowdown, Time Echoes, Timeline Leaping), define: 1) The exact Chrono-Meter cost. 2) The cooldown duration (if any). 3) The specific duration of the effect. 4) The specific thresholds for 'Temporal Entropy' and the exact stat bonuses or enemy spawns that occur at each threshold. This will allow for proper balancing and player understanding.

Reasoning: A game with complex, interconnected systems like time manipulation requires precise rules and clear player feedback. Without specific costs, cooldowns, durations, and entropy thresholds, the mechanics are undefined and cannot be balanced or implemented effectively. This is a critical part of the core gameplay loop.

Weapon Matrix

Severity: Medium

Critique: The GDD provides a list of weapons with their basic stats, but the design is incomplete. The 'Notes' column is vague, and there is no information on how weapon progression works. It is unclear if players start with all weapons or must unlock them, and how their stats might scale or be modified during a run.

Suggestion: For each weapon, expand the 'Notes' to include a brief description of its unique gameplay style or any special effects. Define the full weapon progression system: How are new weapons acquired? Can players upgrade their existing weapons? This will add depth to the combat and player progression.

Reasoning: Weapons are the primary tools for the player's combat, and their design is crucial to the game's feel and replayability. Without specific details on their unique properties and how players obtain and upgrade them, the combat system is incomplete and the player's progression path is undefined.

Temporal Entropy (Debt) System

Severity: Medium

Critique: The GDD mentions that high Entropy triggers 'Anomalous' enemies and increases projectile speeds, but the specific thresholds and the magnitude of these effects are not defined. The system's impact on the player's core abilities is also not fully specified.

Suggestion: Define the exact Entropy thresholds (e.g., 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%). For each threshold, specify the exact percentage increase to projectile speed and the number of 'Anomalous' enemies that spawn. Also, clarify if high Entropy has any negative impact on the player's own Chrono-Meter regeneration or ability costs.

Reasoning: This system is the primary difficulty scaling mechanism for the late game. Without specific thresholds and effects, its impact is vague and cannot be implemented or balanced. Understanding these details is essential for creating the intended challenge curve.

Class-Based Progression

Severity: Medium

Critique: The GDD lists four classes and their basic attributes but does not detail their unique special abilities or how they are unlocked. The 'unlocked_classes' field in the player data structure implies a progression system, but the path to unlocking these classes is not specified.

Suggestion: For each class, define its unique special ability (e.g., a temporary shield, a powerful time-based attack). Then, specify the exact conditions for unlocking each class (e.g., completing a certain number of runs, defeating a specific boss, finding a rare item).

Reasoning: Class diversity and the journey to unlock new playstyles are key components of the roguelike genre. Without specific abilities and unlocking conditions, the classes are undifferentiated, and the player's meta-progression is incomplete.

API Endpoints & Data Structures

Severity: High

Critique: The GDD lists the intended API endpoints and database schema, which is a good start. However, it does not specify the exact data payload for the 'Validated State' update (`PUT /api/runs/{id}`). This is the most critical endpoint for the game's core loop and server-side validation.

Suggestion: Define the specific JSON payload that the client will send to `PUT /api/runs/{id}`. This payload must include all the necessary state information (player position, health, ammo, Chrono-Meter, current room, etc.) and the current run seed for validation.

Reasoning: The 'Validated State' update is the heart of the game's technical implementation for managing time manipulation and ensuring data integrity. Without a defined payload, the server cannot receive or process the necessary information to manage the game state, making the entire system non-functional.
